entries.subject: A false colour from three measured bands, as the HR 8799 planets have
entries.finding: Sanghi et al. (2026) measured this planet with JWST/NIRCam in F410M and F430M, two of the three bands (F410M, F430M, F460M) that colour HR 8799's planets; F460M is not measured, so no comparable three-band colour exists and it is the shared neutral gray.
entries.revisitWhen: Flux densities in three bands comparable with HR 8799's are published.

entries.subject: A second point source inside the planet's Hill sphere
entries.finding: Garza et al. (2026) find that a double point-source fit to the JWST/MIRI 15 micron image is preferred over a single one, most plausibly from systematics; follow-up would be needed to rule out a binary planet. Nothing is drawn.
entries.revisitWhen: Follow-up imaging confirms or rules out a companion of the planet.

entries.subject: The orbit of Matthews et al. (2026)
entries.finding: Matthews et al. (2026) refit the orbit with orvara using a third JWST position (2025 May 10) and publish medians only (a 20.9 au, e 0.244). Their medians miss both JWST positions by about 0.1 arcseconds, 6 to 10 of their errors, so they are not one orbit; Sanghi et al. (2026) publish their posterior, and its best sample is used.
entries.revisitWhen: A fit including all four JWST epochs publishes its posterior.
